findings.issue_text: [BUG] align-items() mixin emits -ms-align-items, which is not a real CSS property; IE10's legacy property is -ms-flex-align, so all consumers of the mixin (header.scss ×2, topic-post.scss ×2) ship invalid dead code into the compiled stylesheet

[ADVISORY] The flexbox mixin stack mixes 2009, 2011, and modern flexbox generations, and on IE10 margin-left: auto and order are not honored by the legacy implementations, causing the header panel to render left-aligned and in DOM order in legacy browsers while appearing to have full legacy coverage

[BUG] .panel { margin-left: auto; } breaks right-alignment in IE10 because IE10's -ms-flexbox does not support auto margins for main-axis distribution; the panel renders inline after the title instead of flush right — a regression from the old float: right which handled IE10 correctly.

[ADVISORY] RTL support silently dropped: float: right mirrored automatically under dir=rtl, but margin-left: auto is a physical, not logical, property, so RTL locales get the panel glued to the left edge, breaking header layout.

[ADVISORY] The align-items mixin emits -ms-align-items, which is not a valid property; the correct old IE syntax is -ms-flex-align, and IE10 also uses a different value vocabulary (start/end vs flex-start/flex-end), so the dead declaration masks intent and may not map values anyway.

[ADVISORY] The .valign-helper inline-block centering hack is retained while align-items(center) now handles vertical centering, leaving dead weight and an unaccounted flex child (order 0) whose width perturbs margin-left: auto spacing; the helper should be removed or given an explicit order.

[ADVISORY] .small-action converted to flex row with no handling for multi-line .small-action-desc content or missing avatar; small-actions without a .topic-avatar collapse to zero leading space and left-align inconsistently with avatar-bearing ones.

[ADVISORY] .extra-info-wrapper is assigned order(2) with no order(1) on .title, relying on default order: 0, while .extra-info-wrapper and .badge-wrapper still use float: left internally — a hybrid float-in-order layout where any future inserted element defaults to order 0 and silently slots between unordered and ordered items.

[BUG] `.small-action-desc` padding rewritten from `0.5em 0 0.5em 4em` to `0 1.5%` with `margin-top: 5px` dropped, causing desc text to overlap the `.topic-avatar` icon at wide viewports and drift at narrow ones — every small-action renders visually broken

[BUG] `p { margin: 5px 0 }` inside `.small-action-desc` changed to `margin: 0` and `> p { padding-top: 4px }` removed, zeroing paragraph spacing so multi-paragraph small-action content stacks flush together

[BUG] Deleting `.bullet { margin-top: 5px; }` on `.extra-info-wrapper .badge-wrapper` misaligns the category bullet with title text; replacing it with `line-height: 1.5` on the whole wrapper is a blunt, differently-scoped compensation that changes line boxes of the title and all badges

[ADVISORY] The `align-items` mixin emits `-ms-align-items: $alignment`, which is not a real property in any IE version, shipping a dead declaration to all callers and misleading signal that old-IE support is covered

[ADVISORY] The mixin passes modern `align-items` keywords straight through to old-spec properties like `-webkit-box-align` which use a different keyword vocabulary (`start`/`end` vs `flex-start`/`flex-end`), so future callers passing `flex-start` silently get no old-Webkit alignment

[ADVISORY] `.panel` gains `@include order(3)` and `.extra-info-wrapper` `order(2)` with no documented requirement for reordering; the `order` mixin emits `-webkit-box-ordinal-group` with a different value scale, and if source order already matches these are inert magic numbers future maintainers must reverse-engineer

[ADVISORY] `.panel` has both `margin-left: auto` and `@include order(3)` doing the same job of pushing the panel right; order(3) is a no-op today while margin does the work, and the two redundant mechanisms will silently conflict if future order values are added.

[ADVISORY] `@include order(2)` on `.extra-info-wrapper` in topic.scss is inert if it isn't a direct child of a flex container, shipping a dead layout directive alongside the effective `line-height: 1.5` change.
[ADVISORY] Flexbox mixins emit obsolete 2009/2012-era vendor prefixes (-moz-box, -ms-align-items, etc.) for long-EOL browsers, shipping 3-5 dead declarations per flex element.

[ADVISORY] `.small-action-desc` visual redesign (padding change from 4em avatar alignment to `0 1.5%`, dropped margin-top, `p { margin: 0 }`) is bundled into a PR labeled as flexbox performance work, landing an unreviewed layout change.

[ADVISORY] Deleting `.title { float: left; }` while making `.contents` a flex container changes the layout model for responsive/mobile header variants not in this diff, with no narrow-width spec coverage.

[ADVISORY] PR stated objective is 'optimize header layout performance' but the diff wholesale rewrites .small-action spacing (removes padding: 0.5em 0 0.5em 4em and margin-top: 5px for padding: 0 1.5%, zeroes paragraph margins, drops padding-top: 4px) — a visual redesign not a header performance change, so intent no longer matches the change and small-action layout renders differently

[BUG] .small-action-desc loses the 4em left padding that compensated for the floated avatar; under the new align-items: center flex row with no gap or spacer, the description text abuts the avatar with only 1.5% padding, rendering flush against the avatar icon instead of indented

[BUG] .contents becomes display: flex with .title and .panel as flex items, but the retained non-absolutely-positioned .valign-helper becomes a flex item that participates in layout, so the helper designed for the old floated layout now visibly occupies a flex slot, changing rendered header height/alignment

[ADVISORY] .extra-info-wrapper .badge-wrapper.bullet { margin-top: 5px } is deleted with no flex-based replacement, so bullet-style category badges in the header lose their vertical offset and badge rows shift vertically — an unintended visual regression; line-height: 1.5 applies to all badge styles and changes every wrapper's box height

[ADVISORY] The flexbox() mixin emits legacy 2009/2012 vendor syntaxes (-moz-box, -ms-flexbox, -webkit-box) unconditionally, but -moz-box/-moz-inline-box and -ms-align-items are dead in browsers supporting modern flex, adding vendor-bloat contrary to the performance claim; also -ms-flex-align: baseline (line 117) uses invalid values for IE10, so that path silently falls back to no alignment

[BUG] mixins.scss ~115: `@mixin align-items($alignment)` emits `-ms-align-items: $alignment;`, which is not a real property in any IE version (IE10/11 use `-ms-flex-align`); the line is dropped by the CSS parser so vertical alignment silently fails in old-IE browsers the prefixed fallbacks exist for

[BUG] mixins.scss ~100: `@mixin inline-flex()` emits `display: -moz-inline-box;` and mixes 2009 vs 2012 spec prefixed variants with different child-box layout semantics, causing `.badge-wrapper.bullet` children to render with mismatched baselines across legacy browsers

[ADVISORY] header.scss 36-37: `.panel { @include order(3); }` with no `order()` on other children makes header layout depend on implicit/explicit ordering spread across two stylesheets; any new child (e.g., plugin outlet element) defaults to order 0 and slots before the title

[ADVISORY] topic-post.scss 279-280: `.small-action` becomes a flex container while `.small-action-desc` padding changes to `0 1.5%` — the percentage padding makes the avatar-to-text gutter vary with container width (~12px difference between widths), and the old explicit value was deleted rather than replaced with a flex gap or margin

[ADVISORY] `@mixin flexbox()` outputs legacy 2009 `-webkit-box`/`-moz-box` and 2011 `-ms-flexbox` declarations unconditionally alongside `display: flex`, so legacy browsers (old Android/iOS Safari, IE10) use the old flex model where children default to no shrink/wrap, breaking the header `.contents` row layout — needs matching `-webkit-box-flex: 0` on children or should drop pre-2012 prefixes

[ADVISORY] `.small-action` was promoted to a flex row but only `.topic-avatar` and `.small-action-desc` are styled; other children (timestamp, delete/small-action controls) become anonymous flex items laid out horizontally, jamming the timestamp into the row instead of its own line

[ADVISORY] `.extra-info-wrapper` gets `@include order(2)` while its child `.badge-wrapper` keeps `float: left`, and removal of the `&.bullet { margin-top: 5px }` compensation combined with the new `line-height: 1.5` means the badge-category text baseline no longer aligns with the `.title` baseline, leaving the category bullet visibly off-baseline

goldens.comment: Mixing float: left with flexbox causes layout issues. Further this PR removes the float-based right alignment for .d-header .panel, which may cause the login panel in the non-Ember/noscript header (where .panel is nested inside .row and not a flex item) to stack under the title instead of remaining right-aligned.

-webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group require values starting from 1, not 0. If $val is 0, this will cause incorrect rendering in older browsers, leading to layout issues.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The flexbox mixin stack mixes 2009, 2011, and modern flexbox generations, and on IE10 margin-left: auto and order are not honored by the legacy implementations, causing the header panel to render left-aligned and in DOM order in legacy browsers while appearing to have full legacy coverage

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new flexbox mixins in `mixins.scss` that explicitly combine 2009 (`-webkit-box`/`-moz-box` + `-webkit-box-align`/`-webkit-box-ordinal-group`), 2011 (`display: -ms-flexbox` + `-ms-flex-align`/`-ms-flex-order`), and modern (`display: flex`, `align-items`, `order`) syntaxes. The header change relies on flex behaviors (`.contents` becomes flex; `.panel` uses `margin-left: auto` and `@include order(3)`) that are not uniformly supported across those older specs, so the concern about “appearing to have full legacy coverage” is grounded in the mixin stack. However, the specific claim about IE10 not honoring `order`/`margin-left:auto` can’t be verified from the diff alone (it’s a browser-compat assertion), so this is better treated as an important compatibility concern rather than a definite, diff-provable bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] .panel { margin-left: auto; } breaks right-alignment in IE10 because IE10's -ms-flexbox does not support auto margins for main-axis distribution; the panel renders inline after the title instead of flush right — a regression from the old float: right which handled IE10 correctly.

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly removes `.panel { float: right; }` and replaces it with a flex layout on `.contents` plus `.panel { margin-left: auto; @include order(3); }`. The claim about IE10 `-ms-flexbox` not supporting main-axis auto margins is a specific browser-compatibility concern tied to this change, but that runtime behavior cannot be verified from the diff alone (no IE10 tests/notes/fallbacks shown).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] RTL support silently dropped: float: right mirrored automatically under dir=rtl, but margin-left: auto is a physical, not logical, property, so RTL locales get the panel glued to the left edge, breaking header layout.

adjudication.rationale: In `header.scss`, `.panel` changes from `float: right;` to `margin-left: auto;` inside a new flex container (`.contents` now includes `@include flexbox()`). `margin-left` is a physical property, so if the project expects RTL mirroring via direction/overrides, this may no longer mirror as intended and could require an RTL-specific override (e.g., swapping to `margin-right: auto`). The diff alone doesn’t prove RTL is broken, but it does introduce a concrete RTL-sensitive change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The align-items mixin emits -ms-align-items, which is not a valid property; the correct old IE syntax is -ms-flex-align, and IE10 also uses a different value vocabulary (start/end vs flex-start/flex-end), so the dead declaration masks intent and may not map values anyway.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `@mixin align-items($alignment)` in `mixins.scss` that emits both `-ms-flex-align: $alignment;` and `-ms-align-items: $alignment;`. The finding is correct that `-ms-align-items` is not a valid IE10/11 flexbox property (the old MS syntax uses `-ms-flex-align`). This is a specific, diff-grounded issue, but the invalid declaration will simply be ignored by browsers, so it’s unlikely to cause broken behavior on its own.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The .valign-helper inline-block centering hack is retained while align-items(center) now handles vertical centering, leaving dead weight and an unaccounted flex child (order 0) whose width perturbs margin-left: auto spacing; the helper should be removed or given an explicit order.

adjudication.rationale: In `header.scss`, `.contents` is changed to a flex container (`@include flexbox(); @include align-items(center);`), while `.valign-helper` is still present in the rule set (its block starts immediately after) and no `order()` is applied to it, whereas `.panel` is explicitly ordered (`@include order(3)`) and positioned with `margin-left: auto`. The diff doesn’t show `.valign-helper`’s actual styles, so the claim that it’s an “inline-block centering hack” and that it definitively perturbs spacing can’t be proven, but it is a concrete, diff-grounded concern that an existing helper element may now be redundant or may need explicit flex ordering under the new flex layout.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] .small-action converted to flex row with no handling for multi-line .small-action-desc content or missing avatar; small-actions without a .topic-avatar collapse to zero leading space and left-align inconsistently with avatar-bearing ones.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `.small-action` to `display: flex` with `align-items: center` and removes the prior `.small-action-desc` left padding (`padding: 0.5em 0 0.5em 4em; margin-top: 5px;`) in favor of `padding: 0 1.5%`. This can reasonably cause alignment/spacing differences when the avatar block is absent or when the description wraps to multiple lines (flex centering vs prior top-aligned flow). However, the diff does not show the HTML structure or confirm that `.small-action` instances can lack `.topic-avatar`, so the specific “missing avatar” case can’t be definitively verified from the patch alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] .extra-info-wrapper is assigned order(2) with no order(1) on .title, relying on default order: 0, while .extra-info-wrapper and .badge-wrapper still use float: left internally — a hybrid float-in-order layout where any future inserted element defaults to order 0 and silently slots between unordered and ordered items.

adjudication.rationale: The diff only adds `@include order(2);` to `.extra-info-wrapper` (topic.scss) and removes a `float` from `.title` while making `.contents` a flex container (header.scss). It does not show `.extra-info-wrapper` being in the same flex context as `.title`, nor does it show the parent of `.extra-info-wrapper` is a flex container or what its siblings’ `order` values are. The claim about relying on default `order: 0` causing new elements to slot “between” items and the referenced missing `order(1)` on `.title` cannot be verified from this diff, and the remaining `float: left` is only on `.badge-wrapper` inside `.extra-info-wrapper`, not evidence of a broken “float-in-order” layout by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] `.small-action-desc` padding rewritten from `0.5em 0 0.5em 4em` to `0 1.5%` with `margin-top: 5px` dropped, causing desc text to overlap the `.topic-avatar` icon at wide viewports and drift at narrow ones — every small-action renders visually broken

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change `.small-action-desc` from `padding: 0.5em 0 0.5em 4em; margin-top: 5px;` to `padding: 0 1.5%` and also makes `.small-action` a flex container (`@include flexbox(); @include align-items(center);`). In a flex layout, the avatar and desc should sit as adjacent flex items, so the old left-padding offset to avoid the avatar is no longer clearly required. The claim that text will overlap the `.topic-avatar` and that “every small-action renders visually broken” is not something that can be verified from the diff alone (no HTML structure, widths, or other relevant styles shown), and the flex change suggests the opposite intent (to prevent such overlap).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] `p { margin: 5px 0 }` inside `.small-action-desc` changed to `margin: 0` and `> p { padding-top: 4px }` removed, zeroing paragraph spacing so multi-paragraph small-action content stacks flush together

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change `.small-action-desc span.first p` from `margin: 5px 0` to `margin: 0` and removes `padding-top: 4px` from `.small-action-desc > p`, which will reduce/eliminiate vertical spacing between paragraphs in that area. However, from the diff alone it’s not verifiable that this is an unintended defect (it may be an intentional layout tweak alongside the new flexbox alignment), so it’s a concrete, diff-grounded UI/spacing concern rather than a clearly provable bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Deleting `.bullet { margin-top: 5px; }` on `.extra-info-wrapper .badge-wrapper` misaligns the category bullet with title text; replacing it with `line-height: 1.5` on the whole wrapper is a blunt, differently-scoped compensation that changes line boxes of the title and all badges

adjudication.rationale: The diff does remove the `.badge-wrapper` `&.bullet { margin-top: 5px; }` rule in `topic.scss` and adds `line-height: 1.5;` to the broader `.extra-info-wrapper`, which will affect line box/vertical rhythm for all its children, not just bullet badges. However, the specific claim that this *misaligns the category bullet with title text* cannot be verified from the diff alone (it depends on runtime layout/markup), so it’s a scope/regression-risk concern rather than a proven defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The `align-items` mixin emits `-ms-align-items: $alignment`, which is not a real property in any IE version, shipping a dead declaration to all callers and misleading signal that old-IE support is covered

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/stylesheets/common/foundation/mixins.scss`, the new `@mixin align-items($alignment)` emits both `-ms-flex-align: $alignment;` and `-ms-align-items: $alignment;`. The latter is not a valid IE/MS flexbox property (IE10/11 use `-ms-flex-align`), so it’s a dead declaration that adds noise and could falsely suggest broader IE support. It doesn’t directly break behavior since browsers ignore unknown properties, but it is a real, diff-grounded issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The mixin passes modern `align-items` keywords straight through to old-spec properties like `-webkit-box-align` which use a different keyword vocabulary (`start`/`end` vs `flex-start`/`flex-end`), so future callers passing `flex-start` silently get no old-Webkit alignment

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `@mixin align-items($alignment)` that blindly assigns `$alignment` to legacy properties like `-webkit-box-align` (in `mixins.scss`). Legacy `-webkit-box-align` uses a different keyword set than modern flexbox (`start`/`end` vs `flex-start`/`flex-end`), so if a caller later uses `@include align-items(flex-start)` it would not map correctly for old WebKit. In this diff, current call sites use `center` and `baseline`, so no broken behavior is directly introduced, but the mixin design creates a concrete compatibility pitfall.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] `.panel` gains `@include order(3)` and `.extra-info-wrapper` `order(2)` with no documented requirement for reordering; the `order` mixin emits `-webkit-box-ordinal-group` with a different value scale, and if source order already matches these are inert magic numbers future maintainers must reverse-engineer

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly adds `@include order(3)` on `.panel` and `@include order(2)` on `.extra-info-wrapper`, and introduces an `@mixin order($val)` that directly maps `$val` to `-webkit-box-ordinal-group`/`-moz-box-ordinal-group` and modern `order`. From the diff alone, there’s no comment or explanation for why these specific order values are needed, so they become “magic numbers” maintainers must infer. Also, the mixin does not account for the historical 1-based `box-ordinal-group` vs 0-based `order` value semantics, which is a concrete cross-browser concern grounded in the emitted properties, but whether it causes broken behavior depends on target browser support not shown in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] `.panel` has both `margin-left: auto` and `@include order(3)` doing the same job of pushing the panel right; order(3) is a no-op today while margin does the work, and the two redundant mechanisms will silently conflict if future order values are added.

adjudication.rationale: In `header.scss`, `.panel` is now a flex item (because `.contents` becomes `display: flex`) and it gets both `margin-left: auto;` and `@include order(3);`. The finding claims these “do the same job of pushing the panel right” and that `order(3)` is a no-op today, but from the diff alone that’s not verifiable: `order` controls the flex item’s ordering among siblings, not its alignment, while `margin-left: auto` is what pushes it to the right. Whether `order(3)` is redundant/no-op depends on the unseen DOM order and other siblings’ `order` values, so the stated redundancy/conflict can’t be confirmed from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] `@include order(2)` on `.extra-info-wrapper` in topic.scss is inert if it isn't a direct child of a flex container, shipping a dead layout directive alongside the effective `line-height: 1.5` change.

adjudication.rationale: The diff only shows `.extra-info-wrapper` gaining `@include order(2);` and `line-height: 1.5;` in `topic.scss`. Whether `order` is inert depends on `.extra-info-wrapper` being a (direct) child of a flex container, but the diff does not show its parent/container styles or relevant markup. Therefore the claim that this directive is definitively dead/inert cannot be verified from the provided changes alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Flexbox mixins emit obsolete 2009/2012-era vendor prefixes (-moz-box, -ms-align-items, etc.) for long-EOL browsers, shipping 3-5 dead declarations per flex element.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces new SCSS mixins in `mixins.scss` (`flexbox`, `inline-flex`, `align-items`, `order`) that output multiple legacy flexbox-era declarations (e.g., `display: -moz-box;`, `display: -ms-flexbox;`, `-ms-align-items`, `-webkit-box-ordinal-group`). These are then used in several stylesheets (`header.scss`, `topic-post.scss`, `topic.scss`, `badges.css.scss`), so the extra prefixed declarations will be shipped per usage. This is a real, diff-grounded maintainability/performance concern (extra CSS/dead declarations), but not a functional defect proven by the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] `.small-action-desc` visual redesign (padding change from 4em avatar alignment to `0 1.5%`, dropped margin-top, `p { margin: 0 }`) is bundled into a PR labeled as flexbox performance work, landing an unreviewed layout change.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does bundle nontrivial layout/visual changes into the same change set as flexbox-related work: in `topic-post.scss` `.small-action-desc` changes from `padding: 0.5em 0 0.5em 4em; margin-top: 5px;` to `padding: 0 1.5%;` and nested `p` margins are changed to `margin: 0`, plus `padding-top: 4px` is removed. These are concrete visual redesign adjustments beyond just introducing flexbox (`.small-action { @include flexbox(); ... }`). While the PR label/motivation can't be verified from the diff alone, the scope-mixing/layout-change aspect is real and review-relevant.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Deleting `.title { float: left; }` while making `.contents` a flex container changes the layout model for responsive/mobile header variants not in this diff, with no narrow-width spec coverage.

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes `.title { float: left; }` entirely and instead makes `.contents` a flex container (`@include flexbox(); @include align-items(center);`). It also changes `.panel` from `float: right` to `margin-left: auto` with `@include order(3)`. This is a substantive layout model change that could affect other header layouts (including responsive behavior), but the claim about specific narrow-width variants “not in this diff” cannot be verified from the provided changes alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] PR stated objective is 'optimize header layout performance' but the diff wholesale rewrites .small-action spacing (removes padding: 0.5em 0 0.5em 4em and margin-top: 5px for padding: 0 1.5%, zeroes paragraph margins, drops padding-top: 4px) — a visual redesign not a header performance change, so intent no longer matches the change and small-action layout renders differently

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly changes `.small-action` layout in `topic-post.scss` (adds flexbox/align-items, changes `.small-action-desc` padding from `0.5em 0 0.5em 4em` + `margin-top: 5px` to `padding: 0 1.5%`, sets nested `p { margin: 0; }`, and removes `padding-top: 4px`), which will alter rendering beyond the header changes in `header.scss`. While the PR’s stated objective can’t be verified from the diff alone, the scope expansion and resulting visual changes in `.small-action` are concrete and review-relevant.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] .small-action-desc loses the 4em left padding that compensated for the floated avatar; under the new align-items: center flex row with no gap or spacer, the description text abuts the avatar with only 1.5% padding, rendering flush against the avatar icon instead of indented

adjudication.rationale: In `topic-post.scss`, `.small-action` is changed to a flex container (`@include flexbox(); @include align-items(center);`). At the same time `.small-action-desc` loses its explicit left offset (`padding: 0.5em 0 0.5em 4em;` is replaced with `padding: 0 1.5%;` and `margin-top: 5px;` is removed). With flex items laid out in a row and no `gap`, `margin-left`, or other spacer added between `.topic-avatar` and `.small-action-desc`, the description content will sit much closer to the avatar than before, potentially appearing flush/insufficiently indented.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] .contents becomes display: flex with .title and .panel as flex items, but the retained non-absolutely-positioned .valign-helper becomes a flex item that participates in layout, so the helper designed for the old floated layout now visibly occupies a flex slot, changing rendered header height/alignment

adjudication.rationale: In `header.scss`, the `.valign-helper` rule remains *outside* the `.contents { ... }` block (it is a sibling selector in the same nesting level), so changing `.contents` to `display: flex` cannot make `.valign-helper` a flex item. The diff shows `.contents` now includes the flexbox mixins, but does not move `.valign-helper` into `.contents` or otherwise make it participate in that flex layout.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] .extra-info-wrapper .badge-wrapper.bullet { margin-top: 5px } is deleted with no flex-based replacement, so bullet-style category badges in the header lose their vertical offset and badge rows shift vertically — an unintended visual regression; line-height: 1.5 applies to all badge styles and changes every wrapper's box height

adjudication.rationale: The diff in `topic.scss` removes the specific rule `&.bullet { margin-top: 5px; }` under `.extra-info-wrapper .badge-wrapper`, and there is no new bullet-specific offset added in that file. The diff also adds `line-height: 1.5;` to `.extra-info-wrapper`, which would apply broadly to its contents unless overridden. However, the claim that this affects “bullet-style category badges in the header” and causes an “unintended visual regression” is not directly verifiable from the diff alone (it’s plausible, but depends on layout/markup not shown).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The flexbox() mixin emits legacy 2009/2012 vendor syntaxes (-moz-box, -ms-flexbox, -webkit-box) unconditionally, but -moz-box/-moz-inline-box and -ms-align-items are dead in browsers supporting modern flex, adding vendor-bloat contrary to the performance claim; also -ms-flex-align: baseline (line 117) uses invalid values for IE10, so that path silently falls back to no alignment

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new flexbox-related mixins in `mixins.scss` that unconditionally emit multiple legacy vendor syntaxes (e.g., `display: -moz-box;`, `display: -webkit-box;`, `display: -ms-flexbox;`, and `-ms-align-items`) in `@mixin flexbox`, `@mixin inline-flex`, and `@mixin align-items`. This supports the finding’s “vendor-bloat” point as a real, diff-grounded concern. However, the claim that `-ms-flex-align: baseline` is definitively invalid in IE10 cannot be verified purely from the diff (we can see `@include align-items(baseline)` in `badges.css.scss`, but IE10 behavior/value support isn’t established by the diff), so it’s not a clearly provable functional bug from the patch alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] mixins.scss ~115: `@mixin align-items($alignment)` emits `-ms-align-items: $alignment;`, which is not a real property in any IE version (IE10/11 use `-ms-flex-align`); the line is dropped by the CSS parser so vertical alignment silently fails in old-IE browsers the prefixed fallbacks exist for

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `@mixin align-items($alignment)` in `mixins.scss` and it indeed emits `-ms-align-items: $alignment;`, which is not a valid IE10/11 flexbox property. However, the same mixin also emits `-ms-flex-align: $alignment;`, which is the actual IE10/11 fallback, so the claim that vertical alignment “silently fails” in old IE is not supported by what’s in the diff. This is still a concrete, diff-grounded issue (invalid CSS output), but not a clearly broken-behavior bug given the correct fallback is present.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] mixins.scss ~100: `@mixin inline-flex()` emits `display: -moz-inline-box;` and mixes 2009 vs 2012 spec prefixed variants with different child-box layout semantics, causing `.badge-wrapper.bullet` children to render with mismatched baselines across legacy browsers

adjudication.rationale: The diff does introduce an `@mixin inline-flex()` that combines legacy 2009-era box model values (`display: -webkit-inline-box;`, `display: -moz-inline-box;`) with 2012+ flexbox values (`-ms-inline-flexbox`, `-webkit-inline-flex`, `inline-flex`). That mixing is visible and could lead to different layout semantics in legacy engines that pick the earlier value. However, the specific claim about `.badge-wrapper.bullet` baseline mismatches across legacy browsers isn’t directly verifiable from the diff alone (no evidence of actual broken rendering is shown).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] header.scss 36-37: `.panel { @include order(3); }` with no `order()` on other children makes header layout depend on implicit/explicit ordering spread across two stylesheets; any new child (e.g., plugin outlet element) defaults to order 0 and slots before the title

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `.contents` becomes a flex container and only `.panel` gets `@include order(3)` plus `margin-left: auto`. No evidence in the diff that ordering is “spread across two stylesheets” or that any other child has an explicit `order()`. Also, a new flex child with default `order: 0` would sort before the `.panel` (order 3), but it would not necessarily “slot before the title” unless the DOM/source order places it before `.title`, which is not shown here. The claimed broken/fragile behavior is not verifiable from this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] topic-post.scss 279-280: `.small-action` becomes a flex container while `.small-action-desc` padding changes to `0 1.5%` — the percentage padding makes the avatar-to-text gutter vary with container width (~12px difference between widths), and the old explicit value was deleted rather than replaced with a flex gap or margin

adjudication.rationale: The diff does make `.small-action` a flex container (`@include flexbox(); @include align-items(center);`) and changes `.small-action-desc` padding from a fixed left gutter (`padding: 0.5em 0 0.5em 4em;`) to percentage-based (`padding: 0 1.5%`). Percentage padding will vary with container width, so the avatar-to-text spacing is no longer fixed and the prior explicit spacing was removed without an obvious replacement like a flex `gap`/child margin in this diff. That’s a concrete, diff-grounded layout concern, but it’s not provably a functional bug from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] `@mixin flexbox()` outputs legacy 2009 `-webkit-box`/`-moz-box` and 2011 `-ms-flexbox` declarations unconditionally alongside `display: flex`, so legacy browsers (old Android/iOS Safari, IE10) use the old flex model where children default to no shrink/wrap, breaking the header `.contents` row layout — needs matching `-webkit-box-flex: 0` on children or should drop pre-2012 prefixes

adjudication.rationale: The diff does add `@mixin flexbox()` that always emits legacy 2009 `display: -webkit-box`/`-moz-box` and 2011 `display: -ms-flexbox` before `display: flex` (see `mixins.scss`), and the header `.contents` is switched from floats to this mixin (`header.scss`). That means older engines that only understand `-webkit-box` will use the legacy box model, which can differ in behavior unless you also supply the corresponding legacy properties on children. However, the specific claim that it *will* break the header row layout due to default shrink/wrap behavior is not directly verifiable from the diff alone (no reproduction/target browser constraints shown).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] `.small-action` was promoted to a flex row but only `.topic-avatar` and `.small-action-desc` are styled; other children (timestamp, delete/small-action controls) become anonymous flex items laid out horizontally, jamming the timestamp into the row instead of its own line

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show `.small-action` being turned into a flex container via `@include flexbox();` and `@include align-items(center);`, but it does not show the HTML structure or what the direct children of `.small-action` are (e.g., timestamp, delete controls). Without the markup, the claim that other children become anonymous flex items and that the timestamp will be “jammed into the row” is speculative and not verifiable from this diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] `.extra-info-wrapper` gets `@include order(2)` while its child `.badge-wrapper` keeps `float: left`, and removal of the `&.bullet { margin-top: 5px }` compensation combined with the new `line-height: 1.5` means the badge-category text baseline no longer aligns with the `.title` baseline, leaving the category bullet visibly off-baseline

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show `.extra-info-wrapper` gaining `@include order(2)` and `line-height: 1.5`, and it removes the `.badge-wrapper { &.bullet { margin-top: 5px; } }` rule while `.badge-wrapper` still has `float: left`. However, the claimed visible baseline misalignment with a `.title` element and the resulting “category bullet off-baseline” is a visual/layout outcome that cannot be verified from this diff alone (no rendering context, no `.title` relationship shown in `topic.scss`).
